activity.title: Current request
activity.empty: Send a message to watch it travel through the pipeline.

chat.placeholder: Ask something. Lists and itemised tasks can be shared with the swarm.
chat.attachHint: Text files up to 200 KB, read on this computer
chat.welcome: Your messages are answered by the models on this computer. With the swarm enabled, itemised requests are split into micro-tasks and shared with other Swarmbly computers.
chat.welcomeHint: Try: Extract one key fact per item from the following list of five items: apples, bridges, comets, drums, electrons. List 5 bullet points, one per item, separately.
chat.deleteBody: It is removed from this computer. Exports you saved are not affected.
chat.exportBody: Choose a format. The file stays on this computer.
chat.agreementTitle: Agreement between replicas is convergence, not correctness.

hint.local: Local: answered on this computer only.
hint.localMulti: Local with several models: itemised requests are spread across your local models; nothing leaves this computer.
hint.lan: Swarm LAN: itemised requests may be shared with authenticated computers on this network. Everything else is answered locally.
hint.auto: Automatic: Swarmbly shares a request only when it splits cleanly and workers are available.
hint.tierLocal: Your privacy tier is LOCAL, so nothing will be sent. Change it in Settings → Privacy to use the swarm.

chat.evidenceTitle: Public context from Wikipedia was added to {n} items; only those items' texts were sent.
chat.lceTitle: The answer used passages from your sources (LCE C1); they did not leave this device.

explore.title: How this answer was made

caveat.verification: Signatures were verified; layer-1 commitments do not exist yet in the protocol and were not simulated.
caveat.agreement: Agreement between models is convergence, not truth: models of different families share errors.
caveat.thresholds: Seam and agreement thresholds are placeholders until calibrated.

explore.agreementNote: Each unit shows how much the replicas agreed. HIGH means they converged; it does not mean the content is correct.
explore.evidenceNote: Public context (Wikidata, Wikipedia CC BY-SA 4.0, PubMed…) added. Only these names were sent:
explore.lceNote: Passages from your sources used in this answer (they did not leave this device):

monitor.title: Swarm
monitor.lede: Computers running Swarmbly on your network. A node counts as authenticated once its identity is proven; announcements are not trusted until then.
monitor.graphLabel: Map of this node and its peers
monitor.graphEmpty: No peers yet. Turn on the local network or connect by address.
monitor.discoveryNote: Each entry records when it was first seen, when an mDNS answer last confirmed it, and when it expires. Entries only refresh when a real answer arrives.
monitor.contributionNote: Work this computer did for others. Your own requests are not counted here.
monitor.lanRefused: You refused local network access. Change it in Settings → Permissions.
monitor.searchOff: Turn on the local network first
monitor.connectBody: Use this when your network blocks discovery. The other computer must run Swarmbly; its identity is verified before anything is exchanged.
monitor.diversityCaveat: More families reduce correlated errors but do not remove them.
monitor.cacheEmpty: Nothing discovered yet. Try Search now.

memory.title: Memory
memory.lede: The Local Cognitive Extension keeps a personal memory on this computer. It is optional and never changes how this computer serves others.
memory.docBody: Your documents stay in a local folder. Answers retrieve from them and the wiki records where every claim came from, so a source can be forgotten completely.
memory.behaviourBody: Style, terminology and procedures can shape requests through a small projection (at most 1 KB) added to the shared contract. Personal fine-tuning (C4) is experimental and off.
memory.notInVersion: Not available in this version of the app.
memory.sourcesBody: Put documents you want Swarmbly to remember in this folder. They are read, never modified.
memory.sourcesOff: Turn memory on to use a source folder.
memory.otherFoldersBody: Folders on this computer that are also read, without copying or changing them (your work documents, for example).
memory.c1Ready: Formats: text, Markdown, Word (.docx), HTML and PDF (with pdftotext). Passages are only used in answers made on this computer and never leave it; a glossary.md file ("term = equivalents") helps across languages.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Every value can be changed and reverted. Defaults favour privacy: nothing is shared until you decide.
settings.moreInAdvanced: More parameters appear with the Advanced profile.

tier.GLOBAL: GLOBAL: authenticated peers may receive fragments

reduce_motion.label: Reduce motion
reduce_motion.help: Turns off pulses and blinking. Your system preference is also respected.

output_dir.label: Output folder
output_dir.help: Where exports and saved reports go. Empty uses the output folder inside your Swarmbly data folder.

model__backend.label: Model runner
model__backend.help: Ollama is recommended. Any OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, vLLM) also works.

model__backend_url.label: Runner address
model__backend_url.help: Leave empty for Ollama on this computer.

model__api_key.label: API key
model__api_key.help: Only for servers that require one. Stored on this computer.

model__model_name.label: Chat model
model__model_name.help: Answers locally, plans and assembles shared answers.

model__multi_model.label: Use several local models
model__multi_model.help: Spread work across local models of different families, and compare their answers when you ask for more than one response.

model__local_models.label: Local models to use
model__local_models.help: Pick at least two of different families.

model__local_parallel.label: Local models at once
model__local_parallel.help: How many local models may generate at the same time. More needs more memory.

model__temperature.label: Temperature
model__temperature.help: Lower is more focused; higher is more varied.

model__max_tokens_per_fragment.label: Fragment length limit
model__max_tokens_per_fragment.help: Maximum tokens each micro-task may produce.

model__embedder.label: Similarity
model__embedder.help: How seams and agreement are measured. Embeddings need an embedding model such as nomic-embed-text.

model__embed_model.label: Embedding model
model__embed_model.help: Name of the embedding model in Ollama.

swarm__lan_enabled.label: Local network
swarm__lan_enabled.help: Announce this computer and find others on this network (mDNS). Nothing is shared without a matching privacy tier.

swarm__k_min.label: Minimum responses per micro-task
swarm__k_min.help: Replicas sent from the start. Two or more give a map of where models disagree, at a proportional cost.

swarm__k_max.label: Maximum responses per micro-task
swarm__k_max.help: Ceiling including extra attempts for slow or failed workers.

swarm__n_fragments_max.label: Maximum fragments
swarm__n_fragments_max.help: Upper bound. The real number comes from the request's structure and the swarm's capacity.

swarm__max_concurrency.label: Micro-tasks in flight
swarm__max_concurrency.help: How many micro-tasks this computer keeps in the swarm at once.

swarm__timeout_ms.label: Micro-task timeout (ms)
swarm__timeout_ms.help: After this, the attempt counts as slow and another worker may be tried.

swarm__worker_enabled.label: Share this computer
swarm__worker_enabled.help: Serve micro-tasks for others with your base models. Your memory and files are never used.

swarm__worker_paused.label: Pause sharing
swarm__worker_paused.help: Keeps the connection but refuses new tasks.

swarm__worker_max_concurrent.label: Tasks at once
swarm__worker_max_concurrent.help: How many micro-tasks you serve simultaneously.

swarm__worker_only_idle.label: Only when idle
swarm__worker_only_idle.help: Refuse tasks while the processor is busy (heuristic).

swarm__worker_only_plugged.label: Only when plugged in
swarm__worker_only_plugged.help: On laptops, refuse tasks on battery.

swarm__hedge_fallback_ms.label: Extra attempt after (ms)
swarm__hedge_fallback_ms.help: Used until enough timings exist; then the observed 95th percentile is used.

swarm__tau_sem.label: Seam threshold τ
swarm__tau_sem.help: Placeholder until calibrated. Below it, a bridge sentence is written.

swarm__discovery_ttl_s.label: Discovery cache lifetime (s)
swarm__discovery_ttl_s.help: Entries without a fresh mDNS answer expire after this.

swarm__p2p_port.label: Swarm port (TCP)
swarm__p2p_port.help: Takes effect after restarting the app. Allow it in your firewall.

privacy__tier.label: Privacy tier
privacy__tier.help: Who may receive fragments of your requests. Requests are always classified on this computer first and can only be made stricter automatically.

privacy__trusted_networks.label: Trusted networks
privacy__trusted_networks.help: Informational only. Being on the same network never implies trust.

results__report_detail.label: Report detail
results__report_detail.help: Minimal reports leave out the text of requests and answers, so they can be shared safely.

results__auto_report.label: Save a report for every shared request

results__keep_stats.label: Keep statistics
results__keep_stats.help: Daily counters for the Swarm view.

evidence__enabled.label: Add public evidence
evidence__enabled.help: In lists of items that name something ("Blue-footed booby", "Ecuador") and in answers on this device that ask for current facts, the app looks the names up in public sources (Wikidata, Wikipedia, PubMed and, if installed, SearXNG) and adds the sentence with the fact. Only item names are sent, never your request or your documents, and nothing if the request is classified as sensitive. It is on by default: in tests it fixed what the models did not know (IUCN status 8/8, event years 5/5) without worsening what they already got right. You can turn it off here.

evidence__timeout_s.label: Maximum time per lookup (s)
evidence__timeout_s.help: If Wikipedia does not answer in time, the item is sent without evidence.

evidence__max_chars.label: Maximum characters per evidence
evidence__max_chars.help: The first two sentences of the entry are cut to this length.

evidence__local_answers.label: Also in answers made on this device
evidence__local_answers.help: When the answer is generated on this device (with your local sources), the app may look up to three names in public sources (Wikidata, Wikipedia, PubMed and, if installed, SearXNG): species, places or programmes your question names, or scientific names found in your sources. Only those names are sent (they are listed in "Explore processing"), never your question or your documents. The answer tells your sources [1] apart from public evidence [W1] and gives both when they differ. Requires public evidence to be on.

evidence__local_max_entities.label: Names looked up per local answer
evidence__local_max_entities.help: Maximum names sent to Wikipedia per answer generated on this device.

evidence__fusion_model.label: Model for answers with evidence
evidence__fusion_model.help: When an answer made on this device combines your local sources with public evidence, a larger local model can write it (slower, better attribution). Other answers keep the conversation's model.

evidence__providers.label: Public sources
evidence__providers.help: One per line, in order of trust: wikidata (structured facts: IUCN status, dates), wikipedia, pubmed (NCBI abstracts of scientific papers) and web (your SearXNG or Google, if you set the URL or the key below). Only names are sent to any of them, never your question or your documents.

evidence__searxng_url.label: Your SearXNG URL
evidence__searxng_url.help: Filled in by the installer below (Install and enable SearXNG). You can also enter the URL of your own SearXNG with JSON output enabled. Needs "web" in the sources.

evidence__google_cse_key.label: Google Custom Search key
evidence__google_cse_key.help: Only if you already had a Google Custom Search JSON API key: the API is closed to new customers and stops working on 1 January 2027. Also needs the search engine identifier and "web" in the sources.

evidence__google_cse_cx.label: Google engine id
evidence__google_cse_cx.help: The "cx" of your Programmable Search Engine.

models.noLicence: Ollama did not report a licence for this model.
models.downloadNote: Models are downloaded by Ollama after you confirm. Suggestions fit this computer's memory.
models.consentBody: Ollama will download this model to this computer.
models.sizeUnknown: reported by Ollama when it starts
models.checkedOn: Size and licence checked on {date}; the licence Ollama reports after downloading is the one that applies.
models.downloadsRefused: Model downloads are off. Change it in Settings → Permissions.

privacy.identityBody: This Ed25519 public key identifies this computer in the swarm. The private key never leaves this computer.
privacy.lanNotTrust: Being on the same network is not trust: every peer proves its identity, and workers never receive the session or your whole request.

lan_discovery.label: Find other Swarmbly computers on this network
lan_discovery.help: Announces this computer with mDNS and listens for others. No other devices are scanned.

model_downloads.label: Allow model downloads through Ollama
model_downloads.help: You still confirm each download after seeing its size and licence.

internet.label: Join swarms over the internet
internet.help: Arrives in Phase 3 with rendezvous servers.

rec.reversible: Applying saves your current settings first. Sharing and the local network are never turned on by a recommendation.

doctor.ollamaPurpose: runs the models on this computer

state.pin_mismatch: differs from the pinned version ({pin}); "Install" updates it

doctor.installBody: They are installed into Swarmbly's own environment with pip. Your system Python is not changed.
doctor.installing: Installing… this can take a few minutes.
doctor.manual: Run this in a terminal (Swarmbly never changes the system Python):
doctor.firewall: If other computers cannot find this one, allow the swarm port (TCP) and mDNS (UDP 5353) in your firewall.

wizard.title: Set up Swarmbly
wizard.welcomeTitle: Your computer, part of a swarm
wizard.welcomeBody: Swarmbly answers with the models on your computer. When you allow it, it splits itemised requests into small tasks that other Swarmbly computers solve in parallel, then assembles the answer here.
wizard.welcomePrivacy: Nothing leaves this computer until you choose a privacy tier that allows it.
wizard.systemBody: Swarmbly needs a few Python packages and a model runner (Ollama).
wizard.profileBody: Based on what was measured. Each value says why; you can change any of them later.
wizard.modelsBody: Models run inside Ollama. Downloads only happen when you confirm them.
wizard.downloadLater: Downloads continue in the background; you can also download later in Settings → Models.
wizard.permBody: Choose what Swarmbly may do on your network. You can change these any time.
wizard.permLater: Allowing the local network does not share anything by itself: sharing also requires a privacy tier and, for others to use this computer, turning on sharing.
wizard.memoryBody: Optional personal memory that stays on this computer.
wizard.memoryLater: More levels are described in Memory.
wizard.doneBody: Swarmbly is set up. The Swarm view shows other computers as they appear, and every answer can be explored step by step.
wizard.answerBoth: Choose Allow or Not now for each question to continue.

websearch.title: Web search (optional)
websearch.body: A free metasearch engine (SearXNG) installed on this computer can query DuckDuckGo, Google, Google Scholar, Bing, Brave, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and Crossref without API keys. It listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1) and starts and stops with the app.
websearch.webOff: "web" is not in Public sources: add it to use this search.
websearch.started: Installing SearXNG; this can take a few minutes
websearch.ready: SearXNG installed and running; "web" was added to public sources
websearch.failed: SearXNG could not be installed; see the details in Settings → Privacy
websearch.noInternet: Internet access is refused in Permissions
websearch.consentBody: SearXNG (AGPL-3.0 licence) and its dependencies, about 60 MB, will be downloaded into Swarmbly's data folder. It will be reachable from this computer only, and "web" will be added to public sources.
websearch.howDocker: Docker is available: the official searxng/searxng image will be used.
websearch.howNative: It will be installed with Python in its own virtual environment (the system Python is not changed).
websearch.howNone: Neither Docker nor Python 3.11 or newer (nor uv) was found. Install one of them and try again.
websearch.consentPrivacy: As with the other public sources, only names (species, places, events) are sent to search engines, never your question or your documents. Some engines (Google, Scholar) may temporarily block automated queries; the others keep answering.
websearch.google: Google: the Custom Search JSON API is closed to new customers and stops working on 1 January 2027. Google and Google Scholar are queried through SearXNG. If you already have a key, enter it below with its "cx" identifier and press "Test web search".

support.title: Support the project
support.body: Swarmbly is developed independently, with no institutional funding, as an AGPL-licensed digital public good. If you find it useful, you can support its early development. Support never buys influence over the roadmap, the licence or the governance.
